extracted.intended_audience: USPTO leadership and staff, trademark and patent examiners, IP policymakers, and external IP stakeholders (practitioners, registrants, and international partners)
extracted.subtask_short: USPTO trademark and IP performance metrics
extracted.subtask_description: Extracted criteria and performance measures used by the USPTO to evaluate trademark examination quality, TTAB operations, IT modernization (TMNG), outreach/education, register integrity, international engagement, and data/transparency efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark First Action Compliance Rate
rubrics_metrics.description: Trademark examination quality is indicated by the first compliance rate, determined through an in‑process review evaluation of the statutory bases for which the USPTO raises issues and/or refuses marks for registration based on the first office action and the examiner’s approval or denial of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported as a percentage with annual targets (example targets shown: 95.5% for FYs 2012–2017). Used to measure accuracy/compliance of the examiner’s initial substantive legal assessment. Data comes from in‑process review evaluations; trend monitoring and target/actual comparisons are used for assessment and improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark Final Compliance Rate
rubrics_metrics.description: Trademark examination quality is also indicated by the final compliance rate, determined by review of the statutory bases for which the USPTO ultimately approves or refuses marks at final disposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported as a percentage with annual targets (example target: 97.0% for FYs 2012–2017). Serves as a measure of final decision accuracy and consistency after prosecution and any applicant responses. Used alongside first action rate to evaluate examiner performance and training needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total Cost Per Trademark Office Disposal
rubrics_metrics.description: A relative measure of efficiency calculated by dividing total expenses associated with the examination and processing of trademarks (including overhead and allocated expenses) by the total number of outputs (office disposals) for the same period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported as dollar amount per disposal with targets and actuals (example targets and actuals provided for FYs 2012–2017). Used to assess cost‑effectiveness of trademark examination process and to inform resource allocation and efficiency initiatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modernize IT Systems (Trademark Next Generation - TMNG)
rubrics_metrics.description: TMNG will separate trademark IT infrastructure from the rest of USPTO IT and implement an integrated end‑to‑end (E2E) electronic processing system for trademark applications and registration maintenance to be faster, more practical, feature‑rich, and more reliable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key success criteria include: user‑centered design (engaging internal/external end users to identify desired features); virtualization and cloud adoption; redesign of ~24 internal systems; replacement of legacy tools (e.g., FAST 1); enhanced functionality for Trademark Status and Document Retrieval (TSDR), X‑search, Electronic Official Gazette, and ID Manual; and delivery of E2E processing. Progress milestones (e.g., FAST1 replacement) and hiring of leadership (Deputy Commissioner) are tracked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stakeholder Engagement for Examination Quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Ongoing engagement with stakeholders (user groups, industry experts, outside lawyers) to validate trademark‑quality findings and provide industry‑specific training and identification updates for goods and services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mechanisms include regular meetings with constituent groups, a customer call center, an email box for customer problems, user‑group training, outside legal CLEs, and working with industry experts. Success measured qualitatively through feedback and used to inform examiner training, identification updates, and examination guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Outreach and Education Effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Outreach activities to practitioners, entrepreneurs, and the public (roundtables, regional video chat sessions, presence at industry events like CES, TORCH training) to expand awareness of trademark processes and protection tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criteria for effectiveness include geographic reach (regional sessions in Detroit, Silicon Valley, Dallas, Denver), interactivity, tailored content for small businesses and entrepreneurs, multilingual materials (videos/booklets in English and Spanish), and audience metrics (e.g., video view counts). Programs are evaluated by attendance, engagement, and stakeholder feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of Pro Bono Trademark Legal Services via Law School Clinics
rubrics_metrics.description: Support for pro bono services through law school clinic program participation (allowing law students to practice before the USPTO under faculty supervision).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program success measured by number of participating law schools (example: expanded to 43) and the benefit to both law students and small business owners represented. Criteria include supervision strictness, educational value, and assistance in filing and obtaining protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark Register Integrity: Post‑Registration Audits and Non‑Use Proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Initiatives to strengthen the integrity and accuracy of the Trademark Register, including random audits of post‑registration filings for proof of use, enhancing declaration solemnity, proposing a permanent random audits program, and developing streamlined non‑use expungement proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation criteria include audit results (e.g., more than half of randomly selected registrants unable to provide proof of use in pilot), publication of NPRMs to make audits permanent, stakeholder‑informed rulemaking, and pilot programs addressing goods/services affected by technological evolution. Goals are to ensure registrations reflect marks actually in use and to provide cost‑effective cancellation mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: TTAB Procedural Efficiency and Rulemaking for Trials/Appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendment of TTAB rules (inter partes/trial proceedings) to streamline trial proceedings and promote efficient and cost‑effective use of Board and party resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criteria include promulgation of Final Rule (effective date tracked), stakeholder outreach (NPRM, roundtables, public comment, public meeting reporting), reductions in average pendency for appeals and trial cases (trend of fifth consecutive year of reduction), transparent reporting of TTAB performance measures, and incorporation of comments into rule drafting. Success measured by pendency declines and stakeholder satisfaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: TTAB Access and IT Improvements (TTABVUE and Legacy Systems)
rubrics_metrics.description: Improve electronic docket and case file repository (TTABVUE) and plan legacy system improvements to support E2E TMNG implementation and provide near‑term functionality enhancements (e.g., bulk download).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criteria include hosting user forums to solicit requirements, developing a legacy improvement package informed by comments, enabling requested features (bulk download of docketed documents), and ensuring compatibility/planning with longer‑term TMNG goals. User feedback and implemented features are primary success indicators.

rubrics_metrics.name: TTAB Practice Guidance and Manual Updates (TBMP and Protective Orders)
rubrics_metrics.description: Regular revision and publication of the Trademark Board Manual of Procedure (TBMP) and Standard Protective Order to reflect statutory and rule changes and to support practitioners and judges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criteria include issuance in searchable/PDF format, incorporation of amendments to the Trademark Act, Trademark Rules of Practice, and Federal Rules of Civil Procedure, timely updates aligned with new procedural rules, publication dates (annual revision), and effectiveness of protective orders (e.g., updated Standard Protective Order effective June 24, 2016).

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic Goal III — Country Action Plan Progress Metric
rubrics_metrics.description: Percentage of prioritized countries for which country teams have made progress on at least 75% of action steps in country‑specific action plans along four dimensions: (1) institutional improvements of IP office administration, (2) institutional improvements of IP enforcement entities, (3) improvements in IP laws and regulations, and (4) establishment of government‑to‑government cooperative mechanisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported as a percentage over fiscal years with trend analysis. Used to assess U.S. leadership and capacity‑building impact internationally. The metric is monitored for trends and variability; additional discussion and country‑level details are available in the report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leadership in International Agreements and Policy (WIPO, PCT, Treaties)
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO role in leading negotiations, preparing ratification/implementation packages (e.g., Beijing Treaty, Marrakesh Treaty), proposing improvements to WIPO/PCT systems, and representing the U.S. in intergovernmental IP fora.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Success criteria include submission of legislative implementation packages to Congress, proposals for electronic document systems and improved prior art searches in PCT, participation and leadership in WIPO standing committees and standards‑setting bodies, and influencing treaty accession/implementation outcomes. Measured qualitatively by negotiation results and implemented proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Educational and Capacity‑Building Program Metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Provision and measurement of domestic and international IP training programs (GIPA/IP Boot Camps, IP capacity‑building for officials, SMEs, students), including counts of programs, attendees, and countries represented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantitative metrics include number of programs (example: 143 training programs in FY2016), attendees trained (example: 7,073 total, with breakdowns), and countries represented (example: participants from 114 countries). Additional measures: reach of distance‑learning modules (unique visitors), multilingual availability, and development of e‑learning/blended learning modules (e.g., trade secret law).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Transparency and Empirical Research Support
rubrics_metrics.description: Enhance access to and transparency of IP‑related data and support empirical research (PatentsView platform enhancements, Patent Examination Research Dataset release, Thomas Edison Visiting Scholars Program).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criteria include releasing datasets in convenient formats for public use and academic research (e.g., Patent Examination Research Dataset covering >9 million applications), enhancing data tools (PatentsView inventor identification and query tools), supporting visiting scholars to produce empirical studies (reports documenting IP’s economic impact), and hosting conferences. Success measured by dataset availability, tool functionality, research outputs, and usage metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work‑Sharing and Patent Prosecution Highway (PPH) Expansion
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursue and expand work‑sharing cooperation programs (PPH, CPC, CSP) that allow applicants who receive a positive ruling on claims in one participating office to request accelerated prosecution of corresponding claims in another office, improving speed and reducing expense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Success criteria include establishing/expanding PPH agreements with other offices (e.g., JPO, KIPO), measurable acceleration of prosecution timelines for participating applications, cost savings for applicants, and leveraging other offices’ work to improve examination efficiency and quality. Monitored via program participation and performance outcomes.
